title: I’m Making a Chaotic Comedy Action Romance Fantasy Visual Novel
author: Sea_Box_4746
selftext:
I’ve been working on a visual novel project recently and wanted to share some of the development process because AI has honestly changed how fast I can prototype ideas.

The game itself is basically a mix of comedy, romance, life-sim systems, and pure chaos. One of the biggest challenges has been making all the mechanics feel connected instead of just throwing random features together.

For example, I’m currently experimenting with:

* affection interactions like headpats/charm events affecting dialogue behavior,
* combat encounters that tie into relationship progression,
* status/money systems where you can build side businesses,
* and choice-based events that permanently change character interactions later on.

What’s been interesting is using generative AI during pre-production to rapidly test dialogue tone, event concepts, UI layouts, and early character ideation before manually refining everything myself. It’s made iteration significantly faster, especially for VN writing experiments where small tone changes completely alter scenes.

Right now I’m mainly focused on writing consistency, UI flow, and finishing the first playable prologue release.

I’m also curious how other people here are using AI in game development without making the final experience feel “AI-generated.” That balance has honestly been the hardest part so far.

The prologue should be releasing soon 👀

comments.author: Agreeable-Safety-360
comments.body: What did you do for the character animation and how did you make it look like it's has a low frame rate?

replies.author: Sea_Box_4746
replies.body:
I use very few frames + longer pauses between them, so the animation looks intentionally low FPS/anime-style 

For example, most expressions only use like 2–4 images:

    image shy_loop:
        "images/characters/shy/1.png"
        pause 0.25
        "images/characters/shy/2.png"
        pause 0.25
        "images/characters/shy/3.png"
        pause 0.25
        repeat
    

I also reuse frames a lot instead of making fully smooth animations. Keeps it lightweight and fits VN aesthetics really well.

replies.author: Agreeable-Safety-360
replies.body: What did you use for the consistency and how many generations did it take you?

replies.author: Sea_Box_4746
replies.body: for consistency just generate a character sheet in your art style including character front view, back view and side views then just upload it to any ai and ask him to create a Jason prompt for your character while keeping everything same from the sheet. Now every time you want to generate anything of that character just edit the Jason prompt and use a reference image of that character

comments.author: flaminghotcola
comments.body: How did you manage to generate different images of the same character and maintain character consistency?

replies.author: Sea_Box_4746
replies.body:
For consistency, first generate a proper character sheet in your art style front view, back view, and side views. Then upload that sheet to an AI model and ask it to generate a detailed JSON character prompt while keeping every design detail consistent.

After that, whenever you want to generate new poses, expressions, or scenes of the character, just reuse that prompt and provide a reference image from the sheet. It helps maintain consistency in hairstyle, clothing, proportions, and overall style across generations.
